source_verification.title: Mutant neurogenin-3 in congenital malabsorptive diarrhea
Permanent neonatal diabetes and enteric anendocrinosis associated with biallelic mutations in NEUROG3

second_answer_attack.resolution: MYO5B disease can cause severe congenital diarrhea, but the biopsy in this item selectively lacks chromogranin-A-positive enteroendocrine cells while absorptive, goblet, and Paneth lineages are preserved; emerging diabetes further points to NEUROG3-dependent endocrine differentiation.

item.lead_in: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
item.tested_construct: Loss of the intestinal SLC26A3 chloride-bicarbonate exchanger impairs chloride absorption and bicarbonate secretion in ileum/colon, causing chloride-rich watery diarrhea, extracellular-volume depletion, hypochloremia, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis.

blind_audit.rationale: NEUROG3 is a basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor required for endocrine-cell development in the intestine and pancreas. Biallelic NEUROG3 defects can cause congenital malabsorptive diarrhea (enteric anendocrinosis) with marked paucity of intestinal enteroendocrine cells and may also produce neonatal or later diabetes. Strongest alternative resolved: MYO5B disease can cause severe congenital diarrhea, but the biopsy in this item selectively lacks chromogranin-A-positive enteroendocrine cells while absorptive, goblet, and Paneth lineages are preserved; emerging diabetes further points to NEUROG3-dependent endocrine differentiation.
